summary.the_pairing_that_matters_most: A row count alone cannot tell a well-run provider from a dead one, and this walk found both extremes sitting next to each other. Lloyds Bank Foundation shows 11 rows and 1 live and is the BEST-maintained provider in the walk: the foundation runs one open programme at a time, says so on its page, and its single live row matches that page exactly on deadline, amount, eligible structures and URL. Power to Change shows 6 rows and 0 live and is also correctly represented: it now describes itself as a think-do tank rather than an open grant-maker, and its funds page 404s. In a spreadsheet these two look identical and both look like failures. One is a provider we track well; the other is an organisation that stopped funding. Any future health metric over the catalogue has to read providers, not counts.
summary.method_note: Three errors today shared one shape, and the shape is worth more than the fixes. A truncated buffer reported four real figures as absent. A guessed domain (bgv.vc, and bbrc.org.uk before it) returned nothing and was briefly read as the provider having nothing. And a check for a quote came back empty because it covered the homepage and /our-offer but not /apply, the page the quote was actually on. grant-tracker-be hit the same family independently, writing three pages to one temporary file in a loop so the last overwrote the evidence for the first. Every one failed towards the answer already in hand. The rule that catches all of them: when a probe comes back empty, the first question is whether the probe worked, and the two cheapest checks are whether the buffer holds the whole page and whether it is the right page.
